title.narrative: Shanxi Energy Efficiency and Environment Improvement Project

description.narrative: The proposed project will improve energy efficiency and reduce emission of greenhouse gases and other pollutants in Shanxi province by introducing and expanding district heating in five urban areas and expanding the coal-mine methane (CMM) gas supply and distribution network in one of these areas. The project follows and complements two previous Asian Development Bank (ADB) projects in the province, which have been completed successfully.

description.narrative: Better air quality and reduced greenhouse gases emission in five urban areas in Shanxi province

By 2018, district heating in the five urban areas reduces aggregate annual coal consumption by 53,493 t, thereby avoiding annual emissions of 133,358 t of CO2, 2,677 t of SO2, 802 t of NOx, 10,534 t of TSP, compared with 2012. Progress/Status: Being achieved. Data Source: Shanxi Province Statistical Yearbook Base year: 2012 Baseline value: N

By 2018, the CMM distribution system in Liulin city reduces annual coal consumption by 31,897 t, thereby avoiding annual emissions of 121,021 t of CO2, 1,444 t of SO2, 1,140 t of NOx, and 5,700 t of TSP, compared with 2012. Progress/Status: Being achieved. Data Source: Project's environmental compliance report 2017 Base year: 2012 Baseline value: N

By 2018, the five urban areas improve their record, by at least 20%, in meeting class IIa air quality standards (2012 baseline - days standards are met during heating season : Jinzhong- 69, Licheng- 68, Qin- 73, Zhongyang- 70, Liulin- 70) Progress/Status: Being achieved. Base year: 2012 Baseline value: N

Output: Energy-efficient district heating in five urban areas Indicator: By 2017, at least 150 staff of executing and implementing agencies are trained, including all female staff directly involved in the project, through six training workshops Progress/Status: The Shanxi PMO offered trainings on ADB Procurement, Contract and Construction Management, Security (Environmental Monitoring), Financial Management and Operation and maintenance and management during 2013 - 2016. The Jinhzong and Qin subproject PMOs have also provided trainings on bill collection, file management and measurement to all staff including all female staff. Licheng subproject provided training for 21 female workers in 2016.

Output: Indicator Indicator: By 2017, modern district heating covering 8.2 million m2, servicing 270,000 urban residents (83,300 urban households, 5,300 of which are poor including 703 households headed by women), and employing 50% women as heating bill collectors is implemented Progress/Status: Central heating subprojects in Jinzhong , Licheng and Qin started trial operation separately from November 2015 and end of 2016. The two other subprojects (Zhongyang and Liulin) will be put into operation in November/December 2017. In jinzhong subproject, it provided heating assistance for 388 low-income households among which about 60 woman-headed households. In Qin subproject, about 200 female headed households were provided heating service in 2016. In Zhongyang subproject, free heating fee for about 30 female-headed households which are vulnerable groups. In Jinzhong subproject 12 out of 13 collectors are female. In Qin subproject, 20 collectors among which 4 person are female. In Licheng subproject, the female collector has been 15. In Zhongyang subproject, by 2017, there will be 50% of the heating fee toll collectors for women. Data Source: Shanxi Province Statistical Yearbook
